Sabzi Polo (Persian Herbed Rice)

Served at: Nowruz

Serves 6-8Prep 30 min (plus 1-4 hours soaking time)Cook 45-55 min

Sabzi Polo is a fragrant and vibrant herbed rice dish, a cornerstone of Nowruz (Persian New Year) celebrations. It symbolizes renewal and the bounty of spring, often served with smoked or fried fish (Mahi) to welcome the new year.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups (600g) Basmati rice
  • 1 bunch (about 2 cups chopped) fresh parsley
  • 1 bunch (about 2 cups chopped) fresh cilantro
  • 1 bunch (about 1.5 cups chopped) fresh dill
  • 1 bunch (about 1 cup chopped) fresh chives or green onions
  • 1/2 teaspoon saffron threads
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) hot water (for saffron)
  • 1/2 cup (115g) unsalted butter, melted, or 1/2 cup (120ml) vegetable oil
  • 2 teaspoons salt (for par-boiling)
  • Water for soaking and par-boiling

Method

  1. Rinse the Basmati rice thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Place the rice in a large bowl, cover with cool water, and add 1 teaspoon of salt. Let it soak for at least 1 hour, or up to 4 hours.
  2. While the rice soaks, prepare the herbs. Wash and thoroughly dry the parsley, cilantro, dill, and chives. Finely chop all the herbs.
  3. Grind the saffron threads into a fine powder using a mortar and pestle or the back of a spoon. Place the saffron powder in a small bowl, add 1/4 cup (60ml) hot water, and let it steep for at least 10 minutes to bloom.
  4. Bring a large pot of water (about 8-10 cups or 2-2.5 liters) to a rolling boil. Add 1 teaspoon of salt. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling water. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the rice grains are elongated and slightly tender but still firm in the center (al dente).
  5. Drain the par-boiled rice in a fine-mesh colander. Rinse briefly with cool water to stop the cooking process and remove excess starch.
  6. Return the pot to medium heat. Add 1/4 cup (60ml) of the melted butter or oil to the bottom of the pot. If desired, arrange a thin layer of potato slices or lavash bread over the butter for an extra crispy tahdig (crispy rice crust).
  7. Gently layer the rice and chopped herbs into the pot. Start with a layer of rice, then sprinkle a generous amount of mixed herbs, then another layer of rice, and so on, finishing with a layer of rice on top. Create a few holes in the rice with the handle of a spoon to allow steam to escape.
  8. Pour the remaining 1/4 cup (60ml) melted butter or oil evenly over the rice. Drizzle half of the bloomed saffron water over the rice.
  9. Cover the pot with a clean kitchen towel (to absorb steam) and then place the lid tightly on top. Cook on medium-high heat for 5-10 minutes until steam builds up, then reduce the heat to low.
  10. Continue to steam for 35-45 minutes, or until the rice is fluffy and the tahdig is golden brown.
  11. Gently scoop the fluffy rice onto a serving platter. Carefully remove the tahdig from the bottom of the pot and arrange it around or on top of the rice. Drizzle the remaining saffron water over a portion of the rice for garnish.

Tips

  • For a richer tahdig, use a thin layer of potato slices or lavash bread at the bottom of the pot before layering the rice.
  • Serve Sabzi Polo with smoked or pan-fried white fish (Mahi) and Kookoo Sabzi (Persian herb frittata) for a traditional Nowruz meal.
  • Avoid stirring the rice too much after adding the herbs to maintain distinct layers and prevent the rice from becoming mushy.
